reasoning_content:
The heredoc terminator `EOF` is at line 108 with leading spaces `      EOF` and, because docker compose folds it, the terminator ended up on the same line as the content. Actually in the YAML the `command: >` folds newlines into spaces, so the whole thing becomes one line except where the `"` quoted string preserves... Actually the command is a folded scalar starting with `sh -c "`. The `>` folds lines. That's why the whole heredoc ended up joined: `...[qonnectra] host=db ... sslmode=disable EOF`. So heredoc never closed.

The clean fix: replace the heredoc block with a `printf` similar to production. Let me rewrite the qgis-server command block in dev compose. I'll replace lines 97-119 (command block) with a printf-based version. Let me view lines 96-119.

Actually, simplest: replace the heredoc with a printf one-liner for pg_service.conf. Let me apply a careful edit using sed is risky. I'll rewrite the block with a Python-free approach — use a here-doc to create the file? I need to modify a YAML file.

Let me just reconstruct the qgis-server service block. I'll use awk/sed. Better: use `ex`/`ed` or perl. Check perl availability.

Actually easiest is to use `sed` to replace lines 100-108 (heredoc) with a printf line. Let me do that.

The command uses `>` folded scalar, so all lines get joined by spaces anyway; a single-line printf is fine.

Replace:
```
        cat > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf <<EOF
      [${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}]
      host=db
      port=5432
      dbname=${DB_NAME}
      user=${QGIS_DB_USER}
      password=${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}
      sslmode=disable
      EOF
```
with:
```
        printf '[%s]\nhost=db\nport=5432\ndbname=%s\nuser=%s\npassword=%s\nsslmode=disable\n' "${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}" "${DB_NAME}" "${QGIS_DB_USER}" "${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}" > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf &&
```

Note: in docker-compose `$` needs `$$` to escape, but the original heredoc used `${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}` unescaped and compose substituted them (we saw values substituted). So keeping single `$` is consistent with existing behavior. Good.

Let me use sed with line range deletion/insertion.

action.command: cd /workspace/deployment && cp docker-compose.dev.yml /tmp/dev.bak && sed -i '100,108c\        printf '"'"'[%s]\\nhost=db\\nport=5432\\ndbname=%s\\nuser=%s\\npassword=%s\\nsslmode=disable\\n'"'"' "${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}" "${DB_NAME}" "${QGIS_DB_USER}" "${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}" > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf &&' docker-compose.dev.yml && sed -n '95,112p' docker-compose.dev.yml
